proof.criterion: A1 - Cache refilling, bus reachable, on the send: a send whose session is in the store but not yet back in this listener's cache succeeds and the message is delivered.
proof.surface: The listener's HTTP send route against a real nats-server (v2.10.22, a JetStream account of the test's own), the target written through a second session registry so this listener's cache has never held it.
proof.observed: --- PASS (0.47s), ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/cmd/listener. The cache is asserted to miss the target immediately before the send; POST /v1/messages/send answers 200 and the envelope is read back off notifications.agent.<id>. Driven again under load in my own probe: 100 concurrent cold-cache sends (50 distinct cold targets plus 50 to one shared cold key, through one trailing listener) were all answered 200, the slowest in 28.4 ms against the 3.5 s send budget, so the read-through neither serialises nor deadlocks on a shared key.
proof.negativeControl: The same handler with liveSessionEntry's read-through removed answers 404 (the implementer's recorded control at 6966043e2904); my own control is the sibling case in the suite, a target nothing ever registered, which stays 404 {"error":"no live session ses_e2e_local_absent"} on the real binary.

proof.criterion: A2 - Cache refilling, on the delivery side: a message already accepted and handed to the delivery path is delivered rather than logged 'not found anywhere', counted skipped and acknowledged away.
proof.surface: The listener's JetStream delivery handler against a real nats-server, the target's record in the session bucket and absent from the delivering listener's cache.
proof.observed: --- PASS (0.05s). Exactly one HTTP push, to the port and session the bucket's record names, and envoy_messages_delivered_total{delivery_status="delivered"} == 1, with the cache asserted to miss the target immediately before the delivery.
proof.negativeControl: Breaking the push on the same path in internal/integration (TestE2E_AgentToAgent_RemoteMachine's record given Port 0) fails that test with 'the remote session was pushed to 0 times, want exactly 1' - so a delivery that pushes nothing is now caught rather than passing silently. Reverted after the run.

proof.criterion: A3 - Bus unreachable: the send is answered rather than left to time out - HTTP 503 naming Envoy's bus, with Retry-After: 1, inside the caller's five-second attempt.
proof.surface: Both. S1: the send route with a TCP relay between it and a real nats-server, cut under the live connection. S2: the real envoy-listener binary with its nats-server stopped under it, driven over curl and through the real @legion/envoy-client.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && ENVOY_TEST_NATS_BIN=/tmp/bin/nats-server go test ./cmd/listener -run '^TestSendAnswersServiceUnavailableWhileTheBusIsUnreachable$' -count=5 -v; and cd packages/envoy && PATH=/tmp/bin:$PATH bash scripts/e2e-local.sh
proof.observed: S1, five consecutive runs rather than one (the architect asked for the bound to be measured, not sampled): 503 in 3.501404137s, 3.500992581s, 3.501488289s, 3.501254726s, 3.501296123s - a 0.5 ms spread on the 3.5 s budget, 1.5 s inside the client's 5 s per-attempt deadline (packages/envoy-client/src/transport.ts), every one carrying 'envoy: the message bus did not answer: bus: waiting for NATS to reconnect: context deadline exceeded' and Retry-After: 1. S2: 'bus-down send: HTTP 503 in 3.502727 seconds' with that body and Retry-After: 1 (out/e2e/bus-down-send-response.json, bus-down-send-headers.txt, bus-down-send-result.txt), and 'EnvoyApiError 503' from createEnvoyClient after its two attempts (out/e2e/bus-down-client-error.json) rather than a timeout; the listener's own log holds one WARN 'listener send' outcome bus_unavailable status 503 per attempt. I also drove the publish route on the same cut connection, which the send tests do not cover: notifications.role.<role> answered 503 in 1.33 ms and 181 microseconds (the role-claim read fails at once on a dead connection, so resolveLiveRoleHolder's two 2 s attempts never accumulate), and a plain notifications.github.* topic answered 503 in 3.501493618s - both inside the caller's 5 s, so the publish route holds the same bound as the send route.
proof.negativeControl: The identical request through the same handler before the relay is cut answers 200 (asserted in the test, and the e2e's accepted send answers 200 before NATS is stopped), so the 503 is the cut's doing and not the rig's.

proof.criterion: A4 - Bus reachable but refusing the publish: the same 503 and the same record carrying the bus's own reason, with 413 for an oversized message and 400 for a subject NATS refuses unchanged.
proof.surface: The send and publish routes against a live, reachable nats-server whose notification stream has been deleted under the running listener.
proof.observed: --- PASS (1.14s). 503 with body 'envoy: the message bus did not answer: nats: no response from stream' and Retry-After: 1, and exactly one WARN 'listener send' with outcome bus_unavailable and status 503.
proof.negativeControl: In the same test against the same stream-less bus, an oversized message still answers 413 with no Retry-After and records outcome too_large, and the topic notifications..x still answers 400 with no Retry-After and records 'listener publish' outcome invalid_request - a handler that answered 503 for every bus error would fail there.

proof.criterion: A5 - Destination genuinely absent: the send is still 404 'no live session <id>', and the delivery path retries, then gives the message up inside a minute, counting it and clearing its attempt entry so the redelivery is not swallowed.
proof.surface: A real JetStream durable consumer over the notification stream on a real nats-server, running the listener's own jetStreamDeliveryHandler, with the server performing the redelivery the handler's NAK asks for; and the real binary for the 404.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && ENVOY_TEST_NATS_BIN=/tmp/bin/nats-server go test ./cmd/listener -run '^(TestUnplaceableAgentDeliveryRetriesThenGivesUp|TestUnplaceableRetryWindowFitsTheBoundsItDependsOn)$' -count=1 -v; and cd packages/envoy && PATH=/tmp/bin:$PATH bash scripts/e2e-local.sh
proof.observed: --- PASS (5.74s) with both subtests, and the arithmetic test PASS (0.00s). First delivery: INFO 'listener agent delivery deferred' reason no_session_record attempt 1, envoy_messages_naked_total == 1, no delivery counter; after the server's redelivery: no 'listener attempt-dedupe skip' line at all, exactly one WARN 'listener agent delivery given up' with reason no_session_record and delivery_status unplaceable_no_record, one unplaceable_no_record increment, no 'skipped' series, one no_holder exception. On the real binary the 404 body is byte for byte {"error":"no live session ses_e2e_local_absent"} (out/e2e/absent-session-response.json).
proof.negativeControl: The sibling subtest with the window at 0 gives the message up on its first delivery - one give-up line, zero deferral lines, no envoy_messages_naked_total series at all - differing from the positive case in one field. I added a second control on the setting itself: the real binary started with ENVOY_UNPLACEABLE_RETRY_WINDOW=not-a-duration wrote exactly one WARN 'invalid ENVOY_UNPLACEABLE_RETRY_WINDOW; using default' carrying value "not-a-duration", ran the whole e2e green on the default, and refused nothing at startup - the behaviour D7 of the plan specifies for a value time.ParseDuration refuses.

proof.criterion: A6 - The record: one line per request naming the destination and the outcome, INFO when accepted and WARN when refused, and a give-up counter label that separates no session record from no push target, and both from skipped.
proof.surface: Both. S1: the two HTTP routes and the delivery handler against a real nats-server, each line read field by field out of the logger's own JSON and each counter read out of the /metrics body. S2: the real envoy-listener binary's own log, out/e2e/listener.log.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && ENVOY_TEST_NATS_BIN=/tmp/bin/nats-server go test ./cmd/listener -run '^(TestListenerRecordsEverySendAndPublishRequest|TestGiveUpCounterSeparatesItsTwoCauses)$' -count=1 -v; and cd packages/envoy && PATH=/tmp/bin:$PATH bash scripts/e2e-local.sh
proof.observed: S1: --- PASS (0.58s) and --- PASS (0.09s). S2, read field by field out of my own run's out/e2e/listener.log rather than by eye: the accepted send is one INFO 'listener send' with outcome "accepted", status 200, target_session "ses_e2e_local", event_id, source "agent", source_session "octocat", payload_summary "Direct acceptance summary."; the refused send is one WARN with outcome "no_live_session", status 404, target_session "ses_e2e_local_absent"; the publish to a role nobody holds is one WARN 'listener publish' with outcome "role_unclaimed", status 404 and no holder field; the accepted role publish is one INFO carrying holder "ses_e2e_local"; each bus-down send is one WARN with outcome "bus_unavailable", status 503. Seven lines, one per request, no line without a request.
proof.negativeControl: Every assertion is 'exactly one line', not 'at least one', so a duplicated or missing record fails it; the two give-up labels are read from a /metrics body taken before and after the deliveries, with the 'skipped' series required to be absent both times, so a label that fell back to skipped fails.

regressionLockAdded.why: The send route's status map has a row no test drove: a session read that did not answer is 503, not 404. Mutating api.go:706 from `errors.Is(err, nats.ErrKeyNotFound)` to `err != nil` - the listener reporting an absence it never checked, which is the incident this issue exists to stop - left `go test ./cmd/listener ./internal/session` entirely green (ok 122.982s / ok 7.180s, the 15 container-only tests skipped). The new test fails under that mutation ('a send whose bucket read never answered: status 404, body {"error":"no live session ses_unanswered_store_read"}') and passes at head (1.57s). It carries its own negative control: the same route and the same unregistered target with the bucket answering is the 404, so the pair differs in one thing only. The mutation was reverted; no production code was changed by this phase.
